reason: The text depicts agency exercised by multiple non-leaders throughout the narrative. Regular Egyptians dig wells seeking water (וַיַּחְפְּרוּ כָל־ מִצְרַיִם סְבִיבֹת הַיְאֹר), Egyptian magicians independently perform their own magical acts (וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵ֛ן חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּלָטֵיהֶ֑ם), and individual servants of Pharaoh make autonomous decisions about protecting their livestock based on fear of God's word (הַיָּרֵא֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָה מֵֽעַבְדֵ֖י פַּרְעֹה). Most significantly, the Israelite people exercise agency by performing the Passover ritual—killing lambs, marking doorways with blood, and preparing to depart—demonstrating that ordinary people, not just leaders, carry out consequential actions that shape events.
